title.narrative: Transport Corridors for Economic Resilience Mozambique SOP 2 Project

description.narrative: Improve regional transport connectivity, climate resilience, and road safety along the Nacala corridor in Mozambique.

The proposed TRACER SOP2 in Mozambique is the second under the TRACER SOP (P180801), which aims to improve efficiency, connectivity and climate resilience of key regional transport and trade corridors in Eastern and Southern Africa. The TRACER SOP2 will support regional transport connectivity along the Nacala Corridor in Mozambique through a combination of physical measures and a comprehensive technical assistance program package. The project will focus on developing climate-resilient road sections, piloting innovative safety and mobility solutions, and promoting corridor-oriented development by enhancing food supply connectivity. At the regional level, it is expected to improve Zambia's and Malawi's access to markets and provide these countries with alternative export/import routes. Under Component 1 (Regional transport connectivity along the Nacala corridor), the project will finance civil works activities that improve the condition, climate resilience and safety of the Nacala Corridor and its secondary network. This component will support: (i) civil works for the upgrade to climate-resilient standards selected secondary roads (R696 between Rapale and Mecuburi (57.26 km) and the N360 between Cuamba and Metarica (67.00 km) to support agricultural production chains and enable year-round connectivity to economic centers along the Mozambican section of the Nacala Corridor, along with supervision, technical audits (including on environmental and social aspects) and Resettlement Plan (RP) implementation; (ii) the enhancement of climate resilience along the corridor through civil works and technical assistance guided by a climate vulnerability assessment, with interventions including slope protection, improved drainage, culverts, bridge reinforcement, nature-based solutions, and a review of existing maintenance contracts to potentially finance targeted maintenance works; and (iii) the enhancement of road safety along the Nacala Corridor through a combination of infrastructure, digital and institutional measures building on iRAP assessments, road safety audits, and stakeholder input; this will include financing the development of an integrated speed management plan for the Nacala corridor, incorporating cost-effective engineering measures (such as well-designed speed humps, roundabouts, raised platform crossings and gateway treatments), along with piloting a post-crash emergency response system, implementing iRAP Star Rating for Schools interventions and financing road safety improvements at eight high-crash locations, as well as feasibility studies for a SMART (Safety, Mobility, Automated, Real-time Traffic Management) corridor concept. Component 2 (Technical assistance program for enhanced logistics and operational efficiency) will finance technical assistance to enable the full regional potential of the Nacala transport corridor and address some of the institutional constraints to regional trade and operational efficiency. The activities will include: (i) enabling multimodality and consolidation hubs, through technical assistance to undertake the preparatory work for interventions that improve multimodality and encourage private sector participation in the logistics operations; (ii) enabling regional coordination through support for the Nacala Development Corridor Management Committee (NDCMC) to strengthen regional coordination, including for the scale-up and implementation of the corridor measurement and monitoring. Component 3 (Project management, monitoring and evaluation) will finance incremental administrative costs for project management to ensure project implementation, and all activities associated with program monitoring and evaluation (M&E) and impact evaluation (IE). Component 4 (Contingent Emergency Response) will facilitate access to rapid financing for emergency response and reconstruction during an eligible crisis, either by a formal declaration of a national or provincial government of emergency or upon a formal request from the Government of Mozambique.
